name: Esplanade des Feuillants
short_description: Wide pathway running along Rue de Rivoli at the north of the Tuileries; named for the Convent of the Feuillants (closed in the Revolution, became a revolutionary clubhouse); planted by Henri IV with mulberries to start a French silk industry.

_pipeline.address: Jardin des Tuileries (Rue de Rivoli side), 75001 Paris
_pipeline.discovery_notes: Created by Le Nôtre for Louis XIV. Named for the Convent of the Feuillants. Originally mulberry-planted by Henri IV for silk; orange-planted after the Revolution; now open for events and statues. Liberty Tree commemorative oak planted 1992.

visit_basis: Wide tree-lined terrace walk running along Rue de Rivoli at the north edge of the Tuileries; you stroll its length past the statues and views, an outdoor promenade with nothing to enter.
opening_hours_basis: A pathway within the enclosed Tuileries garden that closes at night; gated, hours not confidently known; left unfiltered.

opening_hours_basis: A gated underground memorial with seasonal hours; transcribed from its OSM tag whose current (Apr-Sep) window is 'Avr - Sep, Mar-Dim 10:00-19:00' (Mardi-Dimanche, Monday closed) in the tag 'Oct - Mar, Mar-Dim 10:00-17:00; Avr - Sep, Mar-Dim 10:00-19:00'.
